title: Same-target neighbour transport across the primary-gene group boundary
hypothesis: A train-only shrunk neighbour flag-rate beats the degree floor on validate pairs with >=1 neighbour, and the gain decays as similarity loosens from shared gene to shared protein class.
approach: Three similarity tiers (gene, protein-class leaf, protein-class L1), empirical-Bayes shrinkage k=10 toward the condition's train rate, leave-one-drug-out on train rows, HistGBM, AP by neighbour-count bucket.
label: y_faers_signal
split: train/validate, grouped by primary target gene

title: Efficacy label learnability: mechanism features vs indication-encoding features
hypothesis: y_semmeddb_treats is predictable above 3x prevalence from mechanism and target features alone, and the gap to a model including ATC, indication class and drug age measures how much of the signal is 'well-studied drug' rather than biology.
approach: Three designs M / I / M+I with an audited column assignment, HistGBM at 31 leaves, 5 seeds for the AP spread, grouped 3-fold CV in train, one validate pass per design-seed. y_semmeddb_causes carried as an indicative secondary.
label: y_semmeddb_treats
split: train/validate, grouped by primary target gene

title: Degree floor across five FAERS label definitions
hypothesis: Drug degree, condition degree and condition record_count reach AP well above prevalence on y_faers_signal, and their AP ranking is stable across five label definitions.
approach: Train-derived degree terms only. Logistic regression and HistGBM per label variant, plus single-feature fits. Grouped 3-fold CV in train, one validate evaluation.
label: y_faers_signal
split: train/validate, grouped by primary target gene

title: Nested ablation: degree, drug-intrinsic, condition-intrinsic, union
hypothesis: Drug-intrinsic features add >=0.02 AP over the degree baseline, condition-intrinsic features add a further increment, and the no-interaction union falls short of pair-level biology.
approach: Four nested feature designs, one fixed HistGBM, grouped 3-fold CV in train, one validate pass per design, plus a mechanism-subset refit to separate ChEMBL missingness from pharmacology.
label: y_faers_signal
split: train/validate, grouped by primary target gene

title: Two-way-demeaned log PRR residual as the modelling target
hypothesis: Drug and condition intrinsic features predict the degree-free log(faers_prr) residual with Spearman rho >= 0.10 on validate, a larger effect relative to its null than the same features achieve on the binary Evans flag.
approach: Restrict to faers_case_count >= 3. Two-way fixed effects on log PRR by alternating demeaning, fitted on train and applied to validate. HistGBM regressor on the residual, plus the binary classifier on identical rows for a four-cell prediction-vs-target comparison.
label: other
split: train/validate, grouped by primary target gene, case_count >= 3 subset

findings: +0.062 AP (model B vs degree-only A) on the 33.6% of validate pairs with >=1 gene-level train neighbour (conditional AP: A=0.1272, B=0.1889); unconditional AP is diluted by the 66.4% of pairs with no gene neighbour (A=0.1226, B=0.1687). Decay curve by n_neighbours_gene bucket: 0: A=0.120 B=0.158 (n=288357), 1_2: A=0.138 B=0.189 (n=47983), 3_5: A=0.130 B=0.187 (n=35259), 6plus: A=0.118 B=0.190 (n=62552). Tier decay: model B AP on pairs where only class_leaf similarity is available = 0.2016; only class_L1 available = 0.1222 (vs conditional gene-tier AP 0.1889) -- gain does not monotonically shrink as the tier loosens; inspect whether this reflects a class-level effect rather than target-specific pharmacology per the falsification criterion in the spec. Leave-one-drug-out sanity check: train CV AP (0.2796) vs validate conditional AP (0.1889), gap=0.0907 (no sign of self-leakage). Design note: the gene-tier 'primary gene' refinement uses ChEMBL's own disease_efficacy flag to mean 'primary target', not the split's group_key (group_key-based sharing would always be 0 on validate by construction of the grouped split, which would be a degenerate, not a meaningful, feature). Coverage table reproduced on unfiltered edges per the spec's stated measurement method; the gene-tier subunit-expansion exclusion (component_relationship COMPLEX/FAMILY rows) is applied only to the modeling features, not to the coverage reproduction, since the spec describes the coverage numbers as measured before that fix.
next_steps: If the gene-tier gain holds and decays as class-level tiers loosen, proceed to Round 2 pathway-overlap features restricted to target-specific biology. If gain is flat/increasing with looser tiers, redirect toward class-level priors instead.

findings: Residual model: validate Spearman rho=-0.3064 on n=206585 rows (null rho=0). Two-way fixed-effects structure removed R^2=0.4700 of the variance in log(faers_prr) on train, fit by alternating demeaning (train only, applied unchanged to validate; unseen drugs/conditions get offset 0 and are reported as a separate subgroup in <exp_id>_subgroups.csv). Binary comparison on the identical case_count>=3 subset: classifier validate AP=0.4691 vs degree-only baseline AP=0.4301 (prevalence stated in <exp_id>_run_notes.txt). Four-cell trained-on x evaluated-against table is in <exp_id>_target_comparison.csv: compare the residual model's AP against the binary flag and the binary model's Spearman rho against the residual to judge whether the residual model also ranks the flag competitively (the strong result) or only wins on its own target. Recommendation: see <exp_id>_target_comparison.csv and the rho/AP values above for whether later rounds should switch target -- if validate_spearman_residual is near zero while the binary AP clears its baseline by a wide margin, the recommendation is to NOT switch, since the features are predicting reporting structure rather than a degree-free pharmacological signal; if rho clears 0.10 and the residual model also ranks the binary flag competitively, the recommendation is to switch later rounds to the residual target. This subset (47.6% of rows, case_count>=3) is not a random subsample -- it is biased toward well-reported pairs, correlated with drug age and market size, so these numbers are not directly comparable to exp02's headline AP on all rows.
next_steps: Pull results/<exp_id>/ from the bridge-results volume and inspect <exp_id>_subgroups.csv for the case-count-stratum breakdown before generalizing the headline rho -- if signal is concentrated in the 21+ stratum, the 'closer to causal' claim needs that qualifier per the spec's traps section.

findings: Evans-label (y_faers_signal) validate AP is 0.1208 against a validate prevalence of 0.1173 (spec states 11.7%). See exp_20260922_f2c2c3_feature_ranking.csv for which single count (drug_degree, condition_degree, or condition_record_count) carries the most signal per label, and exp_20260922_f2c2c3_ap_table.csv for the logistic-vs-HistGBM AP gap per label (the gap measures how much non-linearity the three counts can support). The single-feature AP ranking did NOT hold across all five label definitions (see feature_ranking.csv for the per-label values and pairwise Kendall tau); the label-definition sensitivity is now mandatory for downstream reporting.
next_steps: If the ranking held, proceed to exp02 (intrinsic feature blocks) reporting against the Evans label only. If it flipped, carry all five label definitions through exp02-exp05.

See <exp_id>_ablation.csv for per-design CV fold spread (min/max) to judge whether each increment exceeds fold-to-fold noise, <exp_id>_subgroups.csv for where the increment concentrates (is_mapped / arm / best_match_tier / has_chembl_match), and <exp_id>_missingness_attribution.csv for whether the drug-side increment survives restriction to the 1,716 mechanism-target ingredients (pharmacology) or collapses (ChEMBL-missingness indicator only). Implication for Round 2's pair-level features stated in that comparison: if the union barely exceeds the degree floor, pair-level biology work is well-motivated; if the union already captures most of the signal, degree plus intrinsics may be essentially all of it.
